title: Ethiopian Spiced Pumpkin Seeds
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Spiced Pumpkin Seeds — raw pumpkin seeds dry-roasted with salt and a pinch of berbere. The harvest season snack made from the seeds left from pumpkin stew preparation — zero waste, high nutrition.
longDesc: Ethiopian spiced pumpkin seeds are the harvest season snack — when pumpkins are cooked for Duba Wat, the seeds are cleaned, dried, and roasted rather than discarded. The berbere touch makes them distinctly Ethiopian.
ingredients: 1.5 cups raw pumpkin seeds — cleaned and dried
steps: Heat dry pan over medium heat.
Add seeds. Roast stirring constantly 12—15 minutes until golden and popping.
Season with salt and berbere while hot.
chefTips: The seeds will start to pop — this is normal and signals they are done.
commonMistakes: Wet seeds — steam instead of roast.
cookingScience: Pumpkin seeds (pepitas) contain exceptionally high zinc — one of the few plant sources of zinc in highly bioavailable form. Roasting increases the Maillard browning on the seed surface without significantly reducing the zinc content.
sustainabilityTips: Roasted pumpkin seeds use what would otherwise be discarded from Duba Wat preparation.
culturalNote: Ethiopian pumpkin seed snack is the harvest season gift — made from the pumpkin seeds that would otherwise be discarded, demonstrating the Ethiopian cooking philosophy that nothing from a prepared ingredient should be wasted.
